title: Maximum Number of Integers to Choose From a Range I
summary: Given an integer array of banned numbers, an integer n , and a maximum sum limit maxSum , determine the greatest number of integers you can select from the range [1, n ] such that none of the selected integers are in the banned list and the sum of the selected integers does not exceed maxSum .
statement: Given an integer array of banned numbers, an integer n , and a maximum sum limit maxSum , determine the greatest number of integers you can select from the range [1, n ] such that none of the selected integers are in the banned list and the sum of the selected integers does not exceed maxSum .
constraints: Select distinct integers from 1 through n that do not occur in banned.
Their total must not exceed max_sum.
Return the maximum possible number selected; duplicate and out-of-range banned values have no extra effect.
reference_solution:
def maximum_allowed_range_count(banned,n,max_sum):
    forbidden=set(banned);total=0;answer=0
    for value in range(1,n+1):
        if value in forbidden:continue
        if total+value>max_sum:break
        total+=value;answer+=1
    return answer

    forbidden=set(banned);total=0;answer=0
    for value in range(1,n+1):
        if value not in forbidden:continue
        if total+value>max_sum:break
        total+=value;answer+=1
    return answer
hints: To maximize how many distinct values fit, always consider allowed values from smallest to largest.
Store banned values in a set so duplicates and membership checks are harmless and fast.
Add each allowed value until the next one would exceed max_sum, then stop.
Replacing any selected larger value with an available smaller value cannot increase the sum, proving the greedy prefix has maximum cardinality.
